mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with falling housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% interacts with a concurrent decline in consumer spending (GDPC1 YoY < 0%) to signal aggressive tightening during a weak demand environment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5 percentage points in a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by > 0.5pp in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal savings (RSAFS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above their respective 12-month averages signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a strengthening manufacturing sector, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
